Summary Description: Elizabeth Kelley is a mathematician with a strong focus in algebraic combinatorics, cluster algebras, and their combinatorial encodings. Her work spans the development of graph LP algebras with positivity results through explicit combinatorial expansions, notably via the introduction of rooted clusters for trees and their associated hypergraph snake graphs and hyper T-paths. She contributes to the broader program of generalized and reciprocal cluster algebras by co-authoring foundational results on generalized cluster scattering diagrams and theta functions, establishing mutation-invariant frameworks and canonical bases for A- and X-type varieties. In related work on skein theory for punctured surfaces, she advances poset-based expansion formulas and skein relations that yield bases (such as bangles and bracelets) under natural topological hypotheses. Across these efforts, Kelley demonstrates a consistent pattern of constructing concrete combinatorial realizations, proving positivity for substantial classes, and forging deep connections between discrete combinatorics and geometric representation-theoretic structures.
